summary: One durable statement closes the run, because the two largest findings share a mechanism and a reader should not have to reconstruct their difference from separate interpretations. The fact records that the same blocking send on the FSM mutation channel is fatal at startup and merely delaying at runtime: at startup the constructor issues it before NewRaft has started the FSM goroutine and before it has returned a handle, so nothing drains the channel and no participant can close the shutdown channel the send also selects on — once the replay needs more batches than the channel holds, the constructor cannot complete, which the retained run showed at the boundary of 128 batches with the blocked stack in the replay path. In the running path the consumer exists and a caller holding the handle can close that channel, so a slow FSM delays the main loop by about one batch at a time — measured as a backlog that stayed within a single entry behind a 25ms Apply, with and without a buffered apply channel. It cites both sides' receipts, and it is the statement I would most want a reviewer to take away, since it explains why one blocking send is a defect and the other is backpressure. That is the end of the run's work: three execution-grounded findings with retained receipts, declared comparisons, witnesses and scoped conditions — the startup replay that blocks NewRaft past the channel's batch capacity, the nonvoter acknowledgement that satisfies VerifyLeader's voter quorum and can accompany committed state the confirming leader never applied, and the membership change that installs a voter immediately against two published descriptions that promise staging — plus five suspicions refuted with evidence rather than argument, one behaviour entry corrected under its own id with its affected use answered, fourteen registered questions all answered, and no necessary gap outstanding. Several of my own earlier readings were narrowed or refuted by their own receipts, and those narrowings remain in the record rather than being tidied away.
